docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Salesforce Platform Development and Integration (PDI) encompasses the comprehensive ecosystem of tools, frameworks, and methodologies for extending Salesforce functionality and seamlessly integrating with external systems. This documentation provides a complete guide for developers, architects, and administrators working with the Salesforce platform.

Key Capabilities:

  • Declarative Development: Build applications using point-and-click tools without writing code
  • Programmatic Development: Create custom solutions using Apex, Lightning Web Components, and other frameworks
  • API Integration: Connect Salesforce with external systems using REST, SOAP, and Bulk APIs
  • Event-Driven Architecture: Implement real-time data synchronization and notifications
  • Security Framework: Robust authentication and authorization mechanisms
  • DevOps Integration: Modern CI/CD pipelines for continuous delivery

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Platform Development
docs.text: Salesforce provides both declarative (low-code/no-code) and programmatic (code-based) development approaches to build custom solutions.

docs.title: Declarative Development
docs.text:
Declarative development enables business users and administrators to build applications using point-and-click tools without writing code.

Lightning App Builder:

  • Drag-and-drop interface: Intuitive visual development environment
  • Lightning components: Pre-built and custom components for rapid application assembly
  • Record pages: Customize object detail pages with flexible layouts
  • App pages: Create custom application pages with dynamic content
  • Home pages: Design personalized user home pages
  • Reusable templates: Save and share page templates across the organization

Flow Builder:

  • Process automation: Automate business processes without code
  • Screen flows: Create guided user experiences with multi-step forms
  • Auto-launched flows: Execute flows automatically based on triggers
  • Scheduled flows: Run flows on a time-based schedule
  • Record-triggered flows: Launch flows when records are created, updated, or deleted
  • Platform events: Integrate flows with event-driven architecture

Custom Objects & Fields:

  • Schema design: Define custom data models for business requirements
  • Custom objects: Create new objects to store specialized data
  • Custom fields: Add fields to standard or custom objects
  • Field types: Text, Number, Date, Picklist, Checkbox, Lookup, and more
  • Relationships: Establish connections between objects
  • Lookup relationships: Loosely coupled references between objects
  • Master-Detail relationships: Tightly coupled parent-child relationships with cascading behavior
  • Formula fields: Calculate values dynamically based on other fields
  • Roll-up summary fields: Aggregate data from child records to parent records

docs.title: Programmatic Development
docs.text:
Programmatic development provides full control over application logic and behavior through code.

Apex Programming Language:

  • Object-oriented programming: Classes, interfaces, inheritance, and polymorphism
  • Triggers: Execute custom logic before or after record operations (insert, update, delete, undelete)
  • Classes and interfaces: Encapsulate business logic and define contracts
  • Exception handling: Manage errors gracefully with try-catch-finally blocks
  • Asynchronous Apex: Execute long-running operations efficiently
  • Future methods: Run processes asynchronously with @future annotation
  • Batch Apex: Process large datasets in manageable chunks
  • Queueable Apex: Chain jobs with more flexibility than future methods
  • Scheduled Apex: Execute Apex at specific times using cron expressions
  • Testing framework: Built-in testing infrastructure for quality assurance
  • Governor limits: Understand and work within platform resource constraints

Lightning Web Components (LWC):

  • Modern JavaScript framework: Built on web standards (ES6+, Shadow DOM, Custom Elements)
  • Web standards-based: Leverage native browser capabilities for optimal performance
  • Component lifecycle: Manage component initialization, rendering, and destruction
  • Data binding: One-way and two-way data synchronization
  • Event handling: Component communication through custom events
  • Salesforce data access: Direct integration with Salesforce objects via wire adapters
  • Third-party library integration: Incorporate external JavaScript libraries

Aura Components:

  • Framework for dynamic web apps: Enterprise-grade component framework
  • Component bundles: Complete packages including controller, helper, and style resources
  • Event-driven architecture: Decoupled communication between components
  • Lightning Data Service: Automatic CRUD operations and caching
  • Component events: Bubble up through component hierarchy
  • Application events: Broadcast events across the entire application

Visualforce:

  • Page-centric development: Traditional server-side rendered pages
  • MVC architecture: Separation of concerns with Model-View-Controller pattern
  • Custom controllers: Implement complex business logic in Apex
  • Standard controllers: Leverage built-in CRUD operations
  • Extensions: Augment standard controllers with additional functionality
  • Component library: Reusable UI components for consistent user experience

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Development Tools
docs.text:
Modern development tools streamline the development lifecycle from coding to deployment.

Salesforce CLI (Command Line Interface):

  • Project scaffolding: Generate project structure with templates
  • Org management: Create, authenticate, and manage Salesforce orgs
  • Metadata deployment: Push and pull metadata between orgs
  • Package development: Build and deploy managed and unlocked packages
  • Scratch org creation: Spin up disposable development environments
  • Data import/export: Manage test data with bulk operations

Developer Console:

  • Real-time debugging: Set breakpoints and inspect execution context
  • Apex execution: Execute anonymous Apex code blocks
  • SOQL/SOSL queries: Test and optimize queries interactively
  • Log inspection: Analyze debug logs with filters and search
  • Checkpoints: Pause execution and examine variable values
  • System overview: Monitor resource usage and performance

VS Code with Salesforce Extensions:

  • Code editing: Advanced IDE features with IntelliSense and code completion
  • Apex language support: Syntax highlighting, error detection, and refactoring
  • Lightning component development: Templates and snippets for LWC and Aura
  • Source control integration: Built-in Git support for version control
  • Deploy and retrieve metadata: Seamless org synchronization
  • Apex test execution: Run and debug unit tests from the IDE

Salesforce DX (Developer Experience):

  • Source-driven development: Version control as the source of truth
  • Scratch orgs: Disposable, configurable Salesforce environments
  • Version control: Git-based collaboration and code management
  • CI/CD integration: Automate testing and deployment pipelines
  • Package development: Create modular, distributable applications
  • Org shape configuration: Define and replicate org configurations

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Integration Fundamentals
docs.text:
Salesforce provides multiple APIs for different integration scenarios and data volumes.

REST API:

  • HTTP methods: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE for standard CRUD operations
  • JSON/XML responses: Flexible data format support
  • OAuth authentication: Secure, token-based authentication
  • API versioning: Maintain compatibility across platform updates
  • Composite requests: Batch multiple operations in a single request
  • Batch requests: Execute multiple sub-requests efficiently

SOAP API:

  • WSDL-based: Contract-first integration with strongly typed schemas
  • Enterprise WSDL: Organization-specific schema for custom objects
  • Partner WSDL: Generic schema for multi-org integrations
  • XML requests/responses: Structured data exchange
  • Session management: Maintain authenticated sessions
  • Query and CRUD operations: Full data manipulation capabilities

Bulk API:

  • Large data operations: Process millions of records efficiently
  • Asynchronous processing: Submit jobs for background execution
  • CSV or JSON formats: Flexible input data formats
  • Job monitoring: Track progress and handle errors
  • Parallel processing: Batch records processed concurrently
  • 2.0 improvements: Enhanced performance and simplified usage

Streaming API:

  • Real-time notifications: Receive updates as data changes
  • PushTopic events: Subscribe to custom queries for specific objects
  • Generic events: Publish and subscribe to custom event messages
  • Platform events: Enterprise-grade event-driven architecture
  • Change Data Capture (CDC): Automatically capture all data changes
  • Long polling: Efficient HTTP-based real-time communication

Metadata API:

  • Deploy and retrieve metadata: Programmatic org configuration management
  • Org configuration management: Automate setup and customization
  • Package deployment: Install and manage packages programmatically
  • Change set automation: Streamline configuration migration
  • Continuous integration: Enable automated testing and deployment

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Integration Patterns
docs.text:
Different integration scenarios require different architectural patterns for optimal performance and reliability.

Request-Reply Pattern:

  • Synchronous communication: Immediate response required
  • Immediate response: Real-time processing and feedback
  • REST/SOAP callouts: Standard HTTP-based integration
  • External services: Declarative integration with REST APIs
  • HTTP callouts: Programmatic API consumption from Apex

Use Case: Credit card authorization, address validation, real-time pricing

Fire-and-Forget Pattern:

  • Asynchronous processing: No immediate response needed
  • No immediate response: Decouple processing from user interaction
  • Outbound messaging: SOAP-based notifications to external systems
  • Platform events: High-volume, scalable event publishing
  • Future methods: Asynchronous Apex execution

Use Case: Order fulfillment, email notifications, audit logging

Batch Data Synchronization:

  • Scheduled data transfer: Regular, time-based data exchange
  • Bulk API usage: High-volume data operations
  • ETL processes: Extract, Transform, Load workflows
  • Data loader: GUI and command-line data import/export tools
  • Middleware integration: Enterprise integration platforms (MuleSoft, Informatica, Dell Boomi)

Use Case: Nightly data warehouse updates, master data synchronization

Remote Call-In Pattern:

  • External systems calling Salesforce: Inbound API requests
  • API authentication: OAuth and session-based security
  • Custom REST/SOAP services: Expose custom endpoints
  • Apex REST: Create RESTful web services with @RestResource
  • Apex SOAP web services: Create SOAP services with webService keyword

Use Case: Mobile app data access, partner portal integration

UI Update Based on Data Changes:

  • Change Data Capture: Real-time notification of all record changes
  • Platform events: Custom event-based data synchronization
  • Streaming API: Subscribe to data change notifications
  • Polling: Periodic queries for data updates (less efficient)
  • Webhooks: HTTP callbacks for event notifications

Use Case: Dashboard real-time updates, external system cache invalidation

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Security & Authentication
docs.text:
Robust security mechanisms protect data and ensure proper access control.

OAuth 2.0 Flows:

  • Web server flow: Traditional three-legged OAuth for web applications
  • User-agent flow: Implicit flow for browser-based applications
  • JWT bearer flow: Server-to-server authentication without user interaction
  • Username-password flow: Direct authentication with credentials (use sparingly)
  • Refresh token flow: Obtain new access tokens without re-authentication
  • Device authentication flow: OAuth for devices with limited input capabilities

Named Credentials:

  • External authentication: Centralized credential management
  • Credential management: Store and manage authentication details securely
  • Certificate-based authentication: Mutual TLS for enhanced security
  • Per-user authentication: Different credentials for each user
  • OAuth configuration: Declarative OAuth setup without code

Remote Site Settings:

  • Whitelist external URLs: Authorize outbound HTTP callouts
  • Callout security: Control which external endpoints can be accessed
  • CSP trusted sites: Content Security Policy configuration

CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing):

  • Browser security: Control cross-origin HTTP requests
  • Trusted origins: Whitelist domains for Lightning Component access
  • Lightning component access: Enable secure cross-domain communication

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Data Integration
docs.text:
Modern data integration approaches enable real-time and virtual data access.

External Services:

  • Schema discovery: Automatically generate Apex classes from API specifications
  • Callout configuration: Declarative REST API integration
  • Flow integration: Use external services in Flow Builder
  • Parameter mapping: Visual mapping between Salesforce and external data
  • Response handling: Automatic parsing and error management

Salesforce Connect:

  • External object access: Query external data as if it were in Salesforce
  • OData protocol: Standard protocol for REST-based data access
  • Cross-org adapter: Access data from other Salesforce orgs
  • Virtual data access: Real-time queries without data replication
  • Real-time data: Always current information without ETL processes

Heroku Integration:

  • Heroku Connect: Bi-directional data synchronization with Heroku Postgres
  • Data synchronization: Real-time or scheduled sync with Salesforce
  • Bi-directional sync: Changes flow between Salesforce and Heroku
  • PostgreSQL database: Leverage relational database capabilities
  • External app hosting: Deploy custom applications on Heroku platform

Event-Driven Architecture:

  • Platform events: Publish-subscribe messaging for loosely coupled integrations
  • Change Data Capture: Automatically publish all data changes as events
  • Event buses: Scalable event delivery infrastructure
  • Pub/sub messaging: Decouple event producers from consumers
  • Event relay: Forward events to external message buses (Apache Kafka, Amazon EventBridge)

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Following best practices ensures scalable, maintainable, and performant solutions.

Development Best Practices:

1. Bulkify Code:

  • Handle collections, not single records: Always process lists of records
  • Avoid single-record operations: Design triggers and methods for bulk processing
  • Use Sets and Maps: Efficiently lookup and deduplicate data

2. SOQL Efficiency:

  • Avoid queries in loops: Execute queries outside loops to prevent governor limit violations
  • Use selective filters: Add WHERE clauses to reduce query size
  • Limit result sets: Use LIMIT clause to retrieve only necessary records
  • Query only required fields: Avoid SELECT * patterns

3. Governor Limits:

  • Stay within limits: Design with platform limits in mind
  • Monitor limits: Use Limits class to track resource consumption
  • Optimize CPU time: Reduce complex calculations and iterations

4. Testing:

  • 75%+ code coverage: Meet minimum requirements with quality tests
  • Test positive and negative scenarios: Verify both success and failure paths
  • Use test data factories: Create reusable test data generation
  • Assert expected outcomes: Validate business logic correctness

5. Error Handling:

  • Implement try-catch blocks: Gracefully handle exceptions
  • Log errors: Record error details for troubleshooting
  • Provide meaningful messages: Help users understand what went wrong
  • Retry logic: Implement exponential backoff for transient failures

6. Asynchronous Processing:

  • Use for long-running operations: Avoid timeout issues
  • Batch Apex for large datasets: Process millions of records efficiently
  • Queueable for chaining: Link multiple jobs with better monitoring
  • Future methods for callouts: Execute HTTP requests asynchronously

Integration Best Practices:

1. API Limits:

  • Monitor and optimize API usage: Track calls against limits
  • Use Bulk API for large datasets: Process millions of records efficiently
  • Implement caching: Reduce redundant API calls
  • Batch requests: Combine multiple operations

2. Authentication:

  • Use OAuth for security: Token-based authentication with refresh capability
  • Named Credentials: Centralized credential management
  • Certificate-based auth: Enhanced security for server-to-server
  • Rotate credentials regularly: Maintain security posture

3. Error Handling:

  • Implement retry logic: Handle transient network failures
  • Exponential backoff: Progressive delay between retries
  • Dead letter queues: Capture failed messages for analysis
  • Alert on failures: Notify administrators of integration issues

4. Idempotency:

  • Design for duplicate prevention: Handle duplicate requests gracefully
  • Use unique identifiers: Track processed requests
  • Implement deduplication logic: Prevent duplicate data creation

5. Logging:

  • Comprehensive error logging: Record all integration failures
  • Include context: Capture request/response details
  • Structured logging: Use consistent log formats
  • Log aggregation: Centralize logs for analysis

6. Rate Limiting:

  • Respect API rate limits: Implement throttling mechanisms
  • Queue excess requests: Buffer requests during high volume
  • Monitor throughput: Track usage against limits

docs.title: CI/CD & DevOps
docs.text:
Modern DevOps practices enable continuous delivery and quality assurance.

Version Control:

  • Git integration: Source control for all metadata and code
  • Branch strategies: Feature branches, trunk-based development, or GitFlow
  • Pull requests: Code review process before merging
  • Code reviews: Peer review for quality assurance
  • Merge conflicts: Resolve conflicts systematically

Continuous Integration:

  • Automated builds: Compile and package code automatically
  • Automated testing: Run unit and integration tests on every commit
  • Validation deployment: Test deployments without committing changes
  • Code quality checks: Static analysis for code standards
  • Static code analysis: Tools like PMD, ESLint for quality enforcement

Continuous Deployment:

  • Automated deployments: Push changes to production automatically
  • Environment promotion: Move changes through Dev → QA → UAT → Production
  • Release management: Coordinate deployments across teams
  • Rollback strategies: Quick recovery from failed deployments
  • Blue-green deployment: Zero-downtime deployments with instant rollback

DevOps Tools:

Open Source:

  • Jenkins: Extensible automation server
  • GitHub Actions: Cloud-based CI/CD integrated with GitHub

Salesforce-Specific:

  • Copado: End-to-end DevOps platform for Salesforce
  • Gearset: Comparison, deployment, and backup tool
  • AutoRABIT: Release management and CI/CD automation
  • Flosum: Git-based DevOps platform

Pipeline Components:

  • Source control trigger: Detect changes in repository
  • Scratch org creation: Provision test environment
  • Test execution: Run automated tests
  • Static analysis: Check code quality
  • Deployment validation: Test deployment without committing
  • Approval gates: Manual review before production
  • Production deployment: Push changes to production org
  • Post-deployment tests: Smoke tests in production
  • Monitoring: Track deployment success and performance

docs.title: Governor Limits
docs.text:
Understanding and working within platform limits is critical for scalable applications.

Synchronous Apex Limits (per transaction):

  • SOQL queries: 100 queries maximum
  • SOSL queries: 20 queries maximum
  • DML statements: 150 statements maximum
  • DML rows: 10,000 rows maximum
  • CPU time: 10,000 milliseconds maximum
  • Heap size: 6 MB maximum
  • Callouts: 100 callouts maximum
  • Callout timeout: 120 seconds maximum

Asynchronous Apex Limits (per transaction):

  • SOQL queries: 200 queries maximum
  • SOSL queries: 20 queries maximum
  • DML statements: 150 statements maximum
  • DML rows: 10,000 rows maximum
  • CPU time: 60,000 milliseconds maximum
  • Heap size: 12 MB maximum
  • Callouts: 100 callouts maximum

Email Limits:

  • Single email invocations: 10 per transaction
  • Mass email invocations: No limit (uses separate email quota)
  • Daily email limit: 5,000 for single emails, 500,000 for mass emails

Platform Event Limits:

  • Publish events per hour: 250,000 (or based on license)
  • Event delivery: At least once delivery guarantee
  • Retention: 24 hours for standard events, 72 hours for high-volume

API Limits:

  • API calls per 24 hours: Based on license type (typically 15,000-100,000+)
  • Concurrent API requests: 25 per org (can be increased)
  • Bulk API batches: 15,000 batches per rolling 24 hours

Strategies to Stay Within Limits:

  • Bulkify your code: Process records in collections
  • Use asynchronous processing: Leverage higher limits for long operations
  • Implement batch processing: Break large operations into chunks
  • Cache data: Reduce redundant queries
  • Optimize SOQL: Use selective queries with indexed fields
  • Use Platform Events: Decouple high-volume operations

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Salesforce Sales Cloud is the world's leading customer relationship management (CRM) platform, designed to help sales teams manage their entire sales process from lead generation to deal closure. As a comprehensive sales automation solution, Sales Cloud provides tools for lead management, opportunity tracking, forecasting, collaboration, and analytics.

Key Value Propositions:

  • 360° Customer View: Unified customer data across all touchpoints
  • Sales Process Automation: Streamline repetitive tasks and workflows
  • Mobile-First Architecture: Access CRM data anywhere, anytime
  • AI-Powered Insights: Einstein AI for predictive analytics and recommendations
  • Scalable Platform: Grows with your business from startup to enterprise

Target Users:

  • Sales Development Representatives (SDRs)
  • Account Executives (AEs)
  • Sales Managers
  • Sales Operations Teams
  • CRM Administrators

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Sales Cloud Architecture
docs.text:
Sales Cloud is built on the Salesforce Platform (formerly Force.com), providing a multi-tenant cloud architecture with robust security, scalability, and customization capabilities.

Core Architectural Components:

  • Multi-Tenant Architecture: Shared infrastructure with data isolation
  • Metadata-Driven Development: Configure without code using declarative tools
  • API-First Design: Comprehensive REST and SOAP APIs for integration
  • Lightning Platform: Modern UI framework with component-based development
  • Einstein AI Layer: Machine learning capabilities integrated throughout

Technical Stack:

  • Frontend: Lightning Web Components (LWC), Aura Components, Visualforce
  • Backend: Apex (proprietary Java-like language)
  • Database: Proprietary multi-tenant database with SOQL/SOSL query languages
  • Integration: MuleSoft, REST/SOAP APIs, Platform Events
  • Security: Role hierarchy, profiles, permission sets, field-level security

Deployment Architecture:

  • Sandboxes: Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, Full Copy
  • Production: Multi-org strategy or single org with business units
  • Mobile: Salesforce Mobile App with offline capabilities
  • Communities: Customer and partner portals

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Core CRM Functionality
docs.text:
Sales Cloud provides comprehensive CRM capabilities that form the foundation of sales operations.

Primary CRM Objects:

  • Accounts: Companies or organizations you do business with
  • Contacts: Individual people associated with accounts
  • Leads: Potential customers not yet qualified
  • Opportunities: Qualified deals in your sales pipeline
  • Quotes: Formal pricing proposals for opportunities
  • Contracts: Customer agreements and terms
  • Orders: Confirmed purchases and order fulfillment
  • Cases: Customer service requests and support tickets
  • Tasks & Events: Activities and calendar items

Data Management Features:

  • Duplicate Management: Prevent and merge duplicate records
  • Data Import: Bulk import via Data Import Wizard or Data Loader
  • Data Export: Weekly export service and manual exports
  • Data Quality: Validation rules, required fields, picklist constraints
  • Record Types: Different page layouts and picklist values per business process

Collaboration Tools:

  • Chatter: Enterprise social network for team collaboration
  • Files: Document management and sharing
  • Notes: Rich text notes attached to records
  • Email Integration: Sync emails with Gmail or Outlook
  • Calendar Sync: Bidirectional calendar synchronization

Search & Navigation:

  • Global Search: Search across all objects and files
  • List Views: Customizable filtered views of records
  • Recently Viewed: Quick access to recent records
  • Favorites: Pin frequently accessed records

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Lead Management
docs.text:
Lead management is the process of capturing, qualifying, and converting potential customers into opportunities.

Lead Capture Methods:

  • Web-to-Lead: HTML forms on your website
  • Email-to-Lead: Convert emails to lead records
  • Manual Entry: Create leads directly in Salesforce
  • Data Import: Bulk import from marketing campaigns
  • API Integration: Real-time lead creation from external systems

Lead Qualification Process:

  • Lead Scoring: Einstein Lead Scoring or custom scoring models
  • Lead Status: Track progression (New → Working → Qualified → Converted)
  • Lead Assignment: Round-robin, territory-based, or queue-based routing
  • Lead Routing: Automated assignment based on rules
  • Lead Nurturing: Automated email campaigns and follow-ups

Lead Conversion:

When a lead is qualified, it converts into three objects:

  • Account: The company (or person account for B2C)
  • Contact: The individual person
  • Opportunity: The potential deal (optional)

Conversion Mapping:

Lead Fields → Target Object Fields
-------------------------------------
Company → Account Name
First Name → Contact First Name
Last Name → Contact Last Name
Email → Contact Email
Phone → Contact Phone

Lead Assignment Rules:

  • Rule Criteria: Based on geography, industry, company size, etc.
  • Queue Assignment: Route to team queues for distribution
  • User Assignment: Direct assignment to specific users
  • Escalation: Automatic reassignment if no action taken

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Opportunity Management
docs.text:
Opportunity management is the core sales process for tracking deals from qualification to close.

Opportunity Stages:

Standard sales stages (customizable):

  • Prospecting: Initial contact and qualification
  • Qualification: Budget, authority, need, timeline (BANT)
  • Needs Analysis: Discovery and requirements gathering
  • Value Proposition: Solution presentation
  • Negotiation/Review: Contract terms and pricing
  • Closed Won: Deal successfully closed
  • Closed Lost: Deal lost to competitor or no decision

Opportunity Fields:

  • Amount: Expected revenue from the deal
  • Close Date: Expected close date
  • Stage: Current position in sales process
  • Probability: Likelihood of closing (stage-dependent)
  • Type: New business, renewal, upsell
  • Lead Source: Origin of the opportunity

Products & Price Books:

  • Product Catalog: Standardized product/service offerings
  • Price Books: Different pricing for different segments
  • Opportunity Products: Line items on an opportunity
  • Quantity & Price: Per-line item configuration
  • Schedules: Revenue and quantity schedules over time

Forecasting:

  • Forecast Categories: Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed
  • Collaborative Forecasting: Manager rollups and adjustments
  • Quota Management: Individual and team quotas
  • Forecast Accuracy: Track prediction vs. actuals

Opportunity Teams:

  • Team Members: Multiple users working on a deal
  • Team Roles: Account Executive, Sales Engineer, Manager
  • Split Credits: Revenue credit distribution
  • Collaboration: Shared visibility and updates

Key Metrics:

  • Win Rate: Closed Won / (Closed Won + Closed Lost)
  • Average Deal Size: Total revenue / number of deals
  • Sales Cycle Length: Days from create to close
  • Pipeline Coverage: Pipeline value / quota
  • Conversion Rate: Opportunities / Leads

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Quote, Contract & Order Management
docs.text:
Sales Cloud provides a complete quote-to-cash process with integrated pricing, contract management, and order processing.

Quote Management:

  • Quote Creation: Generate formal pricing proposals from opportunities
  • Quote Templates: Customizable PDF templates with branding
  • Product Line Items: Add products from opportunity with pricing
  • Discounts & Adjustments: Apply quote-level and line-level discounts
  • Quote Versions: Track multiple versions and revisions
  • Quote Approval: Multi-level approval workflows
  • Quote Sync: Sync quote line items back to opportunity
  • E-Signature Integration: DocuSign, Adobe Sign integration

Quote Fields:

  • Quote Number: Auto-generated unique identifier
  • Opportunity: Associated opportunity (required)
  • Account & Contact: Billing and shipping information
  • Expiration Date: Quote validity period
  • Status: Draft, In Review, Approved, Presented, Accepted
  • Grand Total: Total amount including tax and discounts
  • Primary Quote: Designate as primary quote for opportunity

Contract Management:

  • Contract Records: Formal agreements with customers
  • Contract Terms: Duration, renewal terms, billing frequency
  • Contract Status: Draft, In Approval, Activated, Expired
  • Start & End Dates: Contract lifecycle tracking
  • Contract Line Items: Products/services included
  • Renewal Management: Track renewal dates and opportunities
  • Contract Approval: Automated approval workflows
  • Contract Templates: Standardized agreement templates

Order Management:

  • Order Creation: Convert quotes to orders upon acceptance
  • Order Products: Line items from accepted quote
  • Order Status: Draft, Activated, Completed, Cancelled
  • Activation Date: When order becomes active
  • Order Reduction: Reduce quantities on existing orders
  • Order Amendment: Modify active orders
  • Order-to-Invoice: Integration with billing systems
  • Order Fulfillment: Track delivery and implementation

Quote-to-Cash Flow:

Opportunity → Quote → Contract → Order → Fulfillment

CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote):

For complex pricing scenarios, Salesforce CPQ offers:

  • Product Configurator: Guided selling with product rules
  • Advanced Pricing: Price rules, discounting, and bundles
  • Subscription Management: Recurring revenue and subscriptions
  • Amendment & Renewal: Modify existing subscriptions
  • Contract Lifecycle: Full contract management capabilities

Best Practices:

  • Standardize Quote Templates: Consistent professional appearance
  • Automate Approvals: Route quotes based on discount levels
  • Track Quote Analytics: Monitor quote acceptance rates
  • Integrate with DocuSign: Streamline signature process
  • Use CPQ for Complexity: Complex pricing scenarios require CPQ

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Territory & Quota Management
docs.text:
Territory and quota management ensures fair distribution of accounts and clear revenue targets for sales teams.

Territory Management:

  • Territory Models: Define geographic, industry, or account-based territories
  • Territory Hierarchy: Nested territory structures with inheritance
  • Account Assignment: Manual or rule-based account assignment
  • Opportunity Assignment: Inherit from account territory
  • Territory Forecasting: Forecast by territory hierarchy
  • Territory Handoff: Transfer accounts between territories
  • Territory Analytics: Performance metrics by territory

Territory Assignment Rules:

  • Rule-Based: Assign based on account fields (location, industry, size)
  • Manual Assignment: Direct territory assignment by admin
  • Round-Robin: Distribute accounts evenly
  • Account Matching: Criteria-based matching rules

Quota Management:

  • Quota Types: Revenue, unit, activity quotas
  • Quota Periods: Monthly, quarterly, annual quotas
  • Territory Quotas: Aggregate quotas by territory
  • Team Quotas: Shared team revenue targets
  • Quota Attainment: Track actual vs. quota
  • Quota Adjustments: Mid-period quota modifications
  • Quota Rollups: Hierarchical quota aggregation

Collaborative Forecasting:

  • Forecast Categories: Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed, Omitted
  • Forecast Types: Opportunity revenue, product family, custom
  • Manager Adjustments: Override team member forecasts
  • Forecast Hierarchy: Roll up forecasts through management chain
  • Forecast Submissions: Lock forecasts at period end
  • Forecast Accuracy: Compare predicted vs. actual revenue

Territory Planning:

  • Coverage Analysis: Identify under-covered territories
  • Capacity Planning: Balance territory workload
  • Territory Realignment: Annual territory optimization
  • Split Assignments: Multiple territories for single account

Best Practices:

  • Clear Territory Rules: Minimize overlap and gaps
  • Regular Review: Reassess territories quarterly
  • Fair Distribution: Balance territory potential
  • Transparent Quotas: Clearly communicate targets
  • Track Attainment: Real-time quota performance dashboards

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Sales Automation
docs.text:
Sales automation streamlines repetitive tasks and ensures consistent execution of sales processes.

Workflow Automation:

  • Workflow Rules: IF-THEN logic for field updates, emails, tasks
  • Process Builder: Visual workflow tool with multiple actions
  • Flow Builder: Complex automation with screens, decisions, loops
  • Approval Processes: Multi-step approval routing

Email Automation:

  • Email Templates: Reusable email content with merge fields
  • Email Alerts: Automated emails triggered by workflows
  • Mass Email: Bulk email sending with tracking
  • Email-to-Salesforce: Log emails automatically

Task Automation:

  • Auto-Created Tasks: Workflow-generated follow-up tasks
  • Task Assignment: Automated routing to appropriate users
  • Task Reminders: Automatic notifications before due dates
  • Recurring Tasks: Automatically generate periodic tasks

Einstein AI Automation:

  • Einstein Lead Scoring: Predictive lead quality scoring
  • Einstein Opportunity Scoring: Deal win probability
  • Einstein Activity Capture: Auto-log emails and meetings
  • Einstein Email Insights: Key moment notifications
  • Einstein Forecasting: AI-enhanced forecast predictions

Sales Cadences:

  • Multi-Touch Sequences: Automated call, email, social touch sequences
  • Smart Scheduling: Optimal timing based on engagement data
  • A/B Testing: Test different cadence variations
  • Performance Analytics: Track cadence effectiveness

Automation Best Practices:

  • Start Simple: Begin with basic workflows before complex flows
  • Test Thoroughly: Use sandbox environments for testing
  • Document Logic: Maintain clear documentation of automation rules
  • Monitor Performance: Regular audits of automation effectiveness
  • Avoid Recursion: Prevent infinite loops in automation
  • Bulkify: Design for bulk operations, not just single records

docs.title: Data Model & Relationships
docs.text:
Understanding the Sales Cloud data model is crucial for effective administration and customization.

Standard Object Relationships:

  • Account → Contact: Master-Detail or Lookup (1:Many)
  • Account → Opportunity: Lookup (1:Many)
  • Opportunity → Contact: Opportunity Contact Role (Many:Many)
  • Opportunity → Product: Opportunity Line Item (Many:Many via Products)
  • Account → Case: Lookup (1:Many)

Relationship Types:

  • Lookup Relationship: Loose coupling, independent records
  • Master-Detail Relationship: Tight coupling, child depends on parent
  • Many-to-Many Relationship: Junction object with two master-detail relationships
  • Hierarchical Relationship: Self-lookup (e.g., Account Parent)
  • External Lookup: Relationship to external object

Object Hierarchy:

Account (Company)
├── Contacts (People)
├── Opportunities (Deals)
│   ├── Opportunity Products (Line Items)
│   └── Opportunity Contact Roles (Relationships)
├── Cases (Support Tickets)
└── Activities (Tasks & Events)

Custom Objects:

  • Custom Objects: Business-specific entities (e.g., Projects, Contracts)
  • Custom Fields: Additional fields on standard or custom objects
  • Custom Relationships: Define relationships between custom objects
  • Record Types: Different processes for the same object

Field Types:

  • Text: Single line, multi-line, rich text
  • Number: Integer, decimal, currency, percent
  • Date/Time: Date, datetime, time
  • Boolean: Checkbox
  • Picklist: Single select, multi-select, dependent picklists
  • Lookup: Reference to another object
  • Formula: Calculated field
  • Rollup Summary: Aggregate child records (master-detail only)

Schema Design Best Practices:

  • Normalize Data: Avoid data duplication across objects
  • Use Standard Objects: Leverage existing functionality when possible
  • Plan Relationships: Consider query performance and data hierarchy
  • Field Naming: Use clear, consistent naming conventions
  • Record Types vs Objects: Use record types for variants of same entity
  • Limits Awareness: Stay within Salesforce governor limits

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Administration Best Practices
docs.text:
Effective Sales Cloud administration ensures optimal performance, user adoption, and business value.

User Management:

  • User Licenses: Sales Cloud, Platform, Communities
  • Profiles: Define object and field permissions
  • Permission Sets: Grant additional permissions beyond profile
  • Roles: Define data visibility in hierarchy
  • Public Groups: Group users for sharing rules

Security Model:

  • Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD): Base level of record access
  • Role Hierarchy: Grant access up the hierarchy
  • Sharing Rules: Extend access beyond OWD and role
  • Manual Sharing: Ad-hoc record sharing
  • Team Access: Opportunity teams, account teams

Change Management:

  • Sandbox Strategy: Maintain Dev, QA, UAT, and Prod-like sandboxes
  • Release Management: Structured deployment process
  • Version Control: Use tools like Git for metadata versioning
  • Testing Protocols: Comprehensive test plans before production
  • Rollback Plans: Always have a way to revert changes

Data Governance:

  • Data Quality Standards: Define and enforce data entry rules
  • Duplicate Prevention: Matching rules and duplicate rules
  • Data Retention: Archive or delete old records per policy
  • Backup Strategy: Weekly exports and third-party backup tools
  • Data Privacy: Comply with GDPR, CCPA, and other regulations

Performance Management:

  • Monitor Login History: Track user adoption and activity
  • Review Debug Logs: Troubleshoot errors and performance
  • Storage Management: Monitor data and file storage limits
  • API Usage: Track API calls against limits
  • Health Check: Use Salesforce Optimizer and Health Check tools

Documentation:

  • System Documentation: Architecture diagrams and data models
  • Process Documentation: Business process flows and procedures
  • User Guides: Role-based training materials
  • Admin Runbooks: Standard operating procedures for admins
  • Change Log: Track all configuration changes

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Configuration & Customization
docs.text:
Sales Cloud offers extensive configuration and customization options without code.

Page Layout Customization:

  • Field Arrangement: Organize fields into sections
  • Field Properties: Required, read-only, visible
  • Related Lists: Display child records
  • Custom Buttons: Add actions to layouts
  • Record Type Assignment: Different layouts per record type

Lightning App Builder:

  • App Pages: Build custom page layouts
  • Home Pages: Customize homepage experience
  • Record Pages: Enhance record detail pages
  • Component Library: Drag-and-drop standard and custom components
  • Dynamic Forms: Show/hide fields based on conditions

Validation Rules:

  • Formula-Based: IF-THEN logic to enforce data quality
  • Error Messages: Custom messages displayed to users
  • Error Location: Field-level or top-of-page errors
  • Active/Inactive: Enable/disable rules as needed

Formula Fields:

  • Cross-Object Formulas: Reference parent object fields
  • Text Functions: CONCATENATE, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, UPPER, LOWER
  • Date Functions: TODAY, NOW, YEAR, MONTH, DAY
  • Logical Functions: IF, AND, OR, NOT, CASE
  • Math Functions: ROUND, CEILING, FLOOR, ABS

Custom Buttons & Links:

  • List Button: Action on list view
  • Detail Button: Action on record page
  • JavaScript Button: Execute custom JavaScript (being deprecated)
  • URL Button: Navigate to URL with parameters

Compact Layouts:

  • Key Fields: Display critical info in highlights panel
  • Mobile Optimization: Optimize for mobile experience
  • Chatter Publisher: Fields shown in quick action

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Reporting & Analytics
docs.text:
Sales Cloud provides powerful reporting and analytics capabilities for data-driven decision making.

Report Types:

  • Tabular Reports: Simple list of records
  • Summary Reports: Grouped data with subtotals
  • Matrix Reports: Two-dimensional grouping
  • Joined Reports: Multiple report blocks side-by-side

Report Features:

  • Filters: Criteria to narrow results
  • Grouping: Organize data by fields
  • Formulas: Custom calculated columns
  • Charts: Visual representation of data
  • Conditional Highlighting: Color-code values based on criteria
  • Bucketing: Group values into categories

Dashboard Components:

  • Chart: Bar, column, line, pie, donut, funnel, scatter
  • Gauge: Single metric with ranges
  • Metric: Large number display
  • Table: Data table with rows and columns
  • Lightning Component: Custom component

Analytics Best Practices:

  • Report Folders: Organize by department or function
  • Naming Conventions: Clear, descriptive report names
  • Scheduled Reports: Automate email delivery
  • Dynamic Dashboards: Show data based on viewer
  • Mobile Dashboards: Optimize for mobile viewing

Key Sales Reports:

  • Sales Funnel: Pipeline by stage
  • Win/Loss Analysis: Closed opportunities by outcome
  • Lead Source ROI: Revenue by lead source
  • Sales Rep Performance: Quota attainment by rep
  • Forecast Accuracy: Predicted vs. actual revenue
  • Sales Cycle Length: Time to close by stage
  • Product Performance: Revenue by product

Einstein Analytics:

  • Advanced Visualizations: Interactive charts and graphs
  • Predictive Analytics: AI-powered insights
  • Data Blending: Combine Salesforce and external data
  • Mobile Analytics: Native mobile analytics app
  • Embedded Analytics: Analytics in Lightning pages

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Integration Capabilities
docs.text:
Sales Cloud integrates with numerous third-party systems and platforms.

Integration Methods:

  • REST API: Modern web service API
  • SOAP API: Enterprise-grade web service API
  • Bulk API: Asynchronous processing of large data volumes
  • Streaming API: Real-time event notifications
  • Metadata API: Deploy customizations programmatically
  • Tooling API: Build custom development tools

Common Integration Patterns:

  • Data Synchronization: Bidirectional data sync between systems
  • Data Migration: One-time or periodic data loads
  • Process Automation: Trigger external processes from Salesforce
  • Real-Time Integration: API calls during user interactions
  • Batch Integration: Scheduled bulk data transfers

Popular Integrations:

  • Marketing Automation: Marketo, HubSpot, Pardot
  • Email: Gmail, Outlook, Office 365
  • Calendar: Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar
  • Communication: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom
  • Document Management: DocuSign, Adobe Sign, Box, Dropbox
  • ERP Systems: NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics
  • Customer Support: Zendesk, Freshdesk, ServiceNow

MuleSoft Integration:

  • API-Led Connectivity: System, process, and experience APIs
  • Pre-Built Connectors: 300+ connectors to popular systems
  • iPaaS Platform: Cloud-based integration platform
  • DataWeave: Data transformation language
  • Anypoint Platform: Design, build, manage APIs

AppExchange:

  • Thousands of Apps: Pre-built solutions and integrations
  • ISV Partners: Certified Salesforce partners
  • Free and Paid Apps: Various pricing models
  • Customer Reviews: Community ratings and feedback
  • Security Review: Salesforce-certified security

Integration Security:

  • OAuth 2.0: Industry-standard authorization
  • Named Credentials: Secure authentication management
  • Connected Apps: External app authentication
  • API Security: Field-level and object-level permissions
  • Certificate-Based Authentication: Mutual TLS authentication

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Security & Access Control
docs.text:
Sales Cloud provides enterprise-grade security with granular access control.

Security Layers:

  • Organization Level: Login IP ranges, session settings
  • Object Level: Create, read, edit, delete permissions
  • Field Level: View and edit permissions per field
  • Record Level: OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules

Authentication:

  • Username/Password: Standard authentication
  • Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): REQUIRED by February 2022
  • Single Sign-On (SSO): SAML-based identity federation
  • Social Sign-On: Google, Facebook authentication
  • My Domain: Custom login URLs

Authorization:

  • Profiles: Define user permissions and settings
  • Permission Sets: Grant additional permissions
  • Permission Set Groups: Bundle permission sets together
  • Muting Permission Sets: Temporarily remove permissions

Data Access Models:

Private OWD:

  • Most restrictive
  • Users can only see records they own
  • Access granted via hierarchy, sharing rules, manual sharing

Public Read Only:

  • Users can view all records
  • Can only edit records they own or have been granted access

Public Read/Write:

  • Users can view and edit all records
  • Most permissive model

Sharing Rules:

  • Owner-Based: Share based on record owner
  • Criteria-Based: Share based on field values
  • Manual Sharing: Ad-hoc sharing by users
  • Apex Sharing: Programmatic sharing

Field-Level Security:

  • Visible: Field appears on page layout
  • Read-Only: Field visible but not editable
  • Hidden: Field not visible or editable
  • Sensitive Data: Hide salary, SSN, credit cards

Security Best Practices:

  • Least Privilege: Grant minimum required permissions
  • Regular Audits: Review user access quarterly
  • MFA Enforcement: Require multi-factor authentication
  • Password Policies: Strong passwords with expiration
  • IP Restrictions: Limit login to trusted IP ranges
  • Login Hours: Restrict access to business hours
  • Session Timeout: Automatic logout after inactivity
  • Shield Platform Encryption: Encrypt data at rest

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
Optimizing Sales Cloud performance ensures fast, responsive user experience.

Data Performance:

  • Selective Queries: Filter with indexed fields (Id, Name, OwnerId, RecordTypeId)
  • SOQL Best Practices: Limit results, use WHERE clauses effectively
  • Avoid N+1 Queries: Bulkify Apex code
  • Data Skew: Address large data volumes on single parent records
  • Archive Old Data: Remove or archive inactive records

Page Performance:

  • Lightning Components: Use Lightning Web Components over Aura
  • Reduce Field Count: Show only necessary fields on layouts
  • Minimize Related Lists: Limit number of related lists per page
  • Async Loading: Load heavy components asynchronously
  • Lightning Performance: Use Lightning Performance Analysis tools

Automation Performance:

  • Avoid Recursive Triggers: Implement trigger frameworks
  • Bulkify Code: Handle collections, not single records
  • Limit SOQL Queries: Stay under 100 SOQL queries per transaction
  • Limit DML Statements: Stay under 150 DML statements per transaction
  • Use Platform Cache: Cache frequently accessed data

API Performance:

  • Bulk API: Use for large data volumes (>1000 records)
  • Composite Resources: Batch multiple API calls
  • Query Optimization: Use specific fields, not SELECT *
  • API Limits: Monitor daily API call limits
  • Compression: Enable gzip compression for API calls

Governor Limits:

Key limits to monitor:

  • SOQL Queries: 100 per transaction
  • DML Statements: 150 per transaction
  • Heap Size: 6 MB synchronous, 12 MB asynchronous
  • CPU Time: 10,000 ms synchronous, 60,000 ms asynchronous
  • Callouts: 100 per transaction
  • API Calls: 15,000-1,000,000+ per day (license-dependent)

Monitoring Tools:

  • Debug Logs: Detailed execution logs
  • Event Monitoring: Track login, API, and usage events
  • Salesforce Optimizer: Free performance analysis tool
  • Health Check: Security and performance recommendations
  • Lightning Usage App: Track Lightning adoption

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Sales Cloud supports a wide variety of sales scenarios across industries and business models.

B2B Sales Pipeline Management:

  • Complex Sales Cycles: Multi-month enterprise deals with multiple stakeholders
  • Account-Based Selling: Target and nurture key accounts
  • Committee-Based Decisions: Track multiple contacts and their influence
  • Long Sales Cycles: Manage deals over 6-12+ months
  • High-Value Deals: Enterprise agreements requiring executive involvement

Territory & Quota Management:

  • Geographic Territories: Region-based sales assignments
  • Industry Verticals: Specialized sales teams by sector
  • Account Segmentation: SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise divisions
  • Overlay Teams: Specialists supporting multiple territories
  • Quota Tracking: Real-time attainment monitoring and forecasting

Partner Relationship Management:

  • Channel Partners: Resellers, distributors, VARs
  • Partner Portals: Experience Cloud for partner access
  • Deal Registration: Claim and track partner-sourced opportunities
  • Partner Commissions: Calculate and track partner payouts
  • Co-Selling: Collaboration between direct and partner sales

Sales Performance Analytics:

  • Win/Loss Analysis: Understand why deals close or are lost
  • Sales Velocity: Track speed of deals through pipeline
  • Rep Performance: Individual and team metrics
  • Product Performance: Best-selling products and services
  • Forecast Accuracy: Compare predictions to actual results
  • Pipeline Health: Coverage ratios and stage distribution

Mobile Sales Enablement:

  • Field Sales: Access CRM data on mobile devices
  • Offline Access: Work without internet connectivity
  • Mobile Tasks: Log calls, emails, and meetings on the go
  • Voice Notes: Quick capture of meeting notes
  • Location Services: Check-in at customer locations

Sales Operations:

  • Data Quality: Duplicate management and data cleansing
  • Process Automation: Streamline repetitive tasks
  • Sales Productivity: Tools and workflows to maximize selling time
  • Compliance: Audit trails and approval processes
  • Integration: Connect CRM with ERP, marketing, and support systems

Industry-Specific Use Cases:

Financial Services:

  • Wealth Management: Client portfolio tracking
  • Insurance: Policy sales and renewals
  • Banking: Loan origination and account management

Healthcare:

  • Medical Device Sales: Rep-to-physician relationships
  • Pharmaceutical: Territory management and compliance
  • Hospital Sales: Complex stakeholder management

Technology:

  • SaaS Sales: Subscription-based revenue models
  • Enterprise Software: Complex licensing and renewals
  • Product-Led Growth: Free trial to paid conversions

Manufacturing:

  • Distributor Management: Channel partner relationships
  • Dealer Networks: Multi-tier sales channels
  • Configuration: Complex product configurations

Customer Success Integration:

  • Onboarding Tracking: Post-sale implementation
  • Adoption Monitoring: Product usage and engagement
  • Renewal Management: Subscription renewals
  • Upsell Opportunities: Expansion revenue
  • Customer Health Scores: At-risk customer identification

docs.title: What is Salesforce?
docs.text:
Salesforce is a cloud-based Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform that provides comprehensive tools for sales, service, marketing, and more. It operates on a multi-tenant architecture where multiple customers share the same infrastructure while maintaining complete data separation and security.

Key Benefits:

  • Cloud-Based: No infrastructure management required
  • Scalable: Grows with your business needs
  • Customizable: Extensive configuration and development options
  • Integrated: Connects sales, service, marketing, and analytics
  • Secure: Enterprise-grade security and compliance

docs.title: Salesforce Architecture
docs.text:
Salesforce uses a sophisticated multi-tenant architecture with three main layers:

Architecture Layers:

  • User Interface Layer: Lightning Experience, Salesforce Mobile, APIs for external access
  • Business Logic Layer: Apex code, workflows, validation rules, process automation
  • Data Model Layer: Standard and custom objects, relationships, fields, and metadata

Multi-Tenant Benefits:

  • Cost Efficiency: Shared infrastructure reduces costs
  • Automatic Updates: Three releases per year with new features
  • Resource Optimization: Intelligent resource allocation across tenants
  • High Availability: Enterprise-level uptime and reliability

docs.title: Salesforce Cloud Products
docs.text:
Core Clouds:

  • Sales Cloud: CRM platform for sales teams with lead, opportunity, and account management
  • Service Cloud: Customer service and support with case management and knowledge base
  • Marketing Cloud: Marketing automation, email campaigns, and customer journey management
  • Commerce Cloud: E-commerce platform for B2C and B2B online stores
  • Experience Cloud: Build branded portals and communities for customers and partners
  • Analytics Cloud (Tableau CRM): Business intelligence and advanced analytics
  • Industry Clouds: Specialized solutions for Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, and more

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Standard vs Custom Objects
docs.text:
Standard Objects:

  • Definition: Pre-built objects provided by Salesforce
  • Examples: Account, Contact, Opportunity, Case, Lead, Campaign
  • Naming: Fixed names defined by Salesforce
  • Features: Come with standard fields, page layouts, and functionality
  • Relationship: Can be extended but not deleted

Custom Objects:

  • Definition: Created by users to store organization-specific data
  • Naming Convention: Always end with __c suffix (e.g., Invoice__c)
  • Flexibility: Fully customizable fields, relationships, and behaviors
  • Use Cases: Store unique business data not covered by standard objects
  • Limits: Varies by Salesforce edition

docs.title: Relationship Types
docs.text:
Understanding relationships is crucial for data modeling in Salesforce:

Lookup Relationship:

  • Coupling: Loosely coupled, independent records
  • Delete Behavior: No cascade delete (child remains if parent deleted)
  • Sharing: Child records have independent sharing
  • Roll-Up Summaries: Not available
  • Use Case: Optional associations between objects

Master-Detail Relationship:

  • Coupling: Tightly coupled, detail depends on master
  • Delete Behavior: Cascade delete (child deleted when parent deleted)
  • Sharing: Child inherits sharing from master
  • Roll-Up Summaries: Available on master side
  • Ownership: Detail records owned by master record owner
  • Use Case: Strong parent-child relationships

Many-to-Many Relationship:

  • Implementation: Junction object with two master-detail relationships
  • Example: Students and Classes connected via Enrollment object
  • Flexibility: Supports complex data models
  • Reporting: Enables relationship-based queries

External Lookup:

  • Purpose: Relates to external objects (Salesforce Connect)
  • Data Location: Data stored outside Salesforce
  • Real-Time: Accesses external data in real-time

Hierarchical Relationship:

  • Availability: User and Account objects only
  • Purpose: Self-referencing relationships (e.g., User reports to User)
  • Depth: Up to 20 levels in hierarchy

docs.title: Formula Fields vs Roll-Up Summary Fields
docs.text:
Formula Field:

  • Calculation: Real-time calculation using other fields
  • Data Type: Various types (Number, Text, Date, Checkbox)
  • Availability: Any object type
  • Storage: Not stored, calculated on-the-fly
  • Governor Limits: Counts against formula evaluation limits
  • Use Cases: Concatenations, calculations, conditional logic

Example Formula:

IF(Amount > 100000, "High Value", "Standard")

Roll-Up Summary Field:

  • Aggregation: SUM, COUNT, MIN, MAX of child records
  • Availability: Only on master side of master-detail
  • Storage: Stored value, updated when child changes
  • Filters: Can include filter criteria
  • Performance: Better for reporting than formula fields

Example Roll-Up:

SUM(Opportunity.Amount WHERE Stage = "Closed Won")

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Salesforce Security Layers
docs.text:
Salesforce implements a comprehensive multi-layered security model:

Security Model Hierarchy:

  1. Organization-Level Security: Login IP ranges, session settings, password policies
  2. Object-Level Security: CRUD permissions via profiles and permission sets
  3. Field-Level Security (FLS): Field visibility and editability controls
  4. Record-Level Security: OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual sharing

docs.title: Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD)
docs.text:
OWD defines the baseline access level for records:

Access Levels:

  • Private: Only record owner and users above in role hierarchy can access
  • Public Read Only: All users can view but not edit
  • Public Read/Write: All users can view and edit
  • Public Read/Write/Transfer: Available for Leads, Cases, and Campaigns
  • Controlled by Parent: For detail in master-detail relationship

Best Practice: Start with most restrictive OWD, then open up access using sharing rules.

docs.title: Profiles vs Permission Sets
docs.text:
Profile:

  • Assignment: One profile per user (mandatory)
  • Purpose: Defines baseline permissions and access
  • Controls: Object permissions, field permissions, app visibility, tab settings
  • Limitation: Cannot grant permissions beyond profile
  • Management: System Administrator, Standard User, etc.

Permission Set:

  • Assignment: Zero or more per user (optional)
  • Purpose: Extends profile by granting additional permissions
  • Flexibility: Modular approach to permission management
  • Use Case: Grant special permissions to subset of users
  • Example: Grant "Delete Cases" to specific support agents

Permission Set Group:

  • Bundling: Groups multiple permission sets together
  • Simplification: Assign multiple permissions at once
  • Management: Easier permission administration

When to Use:

  • Profile: Define role-based baseline permissions
  • Permission Set: Grant additional permissions for specific tasks or projects
  • Permission Set Group: Manage complex permission combinations

docs.title: Sharing Rules
docs.text:
Types of Sharing Rules:

  • Owner-Based: Share records owned by certain users
  • Criteria-Based: Share records meeting specific criteria
  • Guest User Sharing Rules: For Experience Cloud sites

Recalculation:

  • Automatic: When rules change
  • Manual: Recalculate button for on-demand updates

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Salesforce Automation Options
docs.text:
Salesforce provides multiple automation tools for different use cases:

Tool Comparison:

  • Flow: Most powerful, supports screen flows and auto-launched flows
  • Process Builder: Legacy tool being replaced by Flow
  • Workflow Rules: Simple field updates and email alerts (legacy)
  • Approval Processes: Multi-step approval workflows
  • Apex Triggers: Code-based automation for complex logic

docs.title: When to Use Flow vs Apex Trigger
docs.text:
Use Flow When:

  • No-Code Solution: Business logic can be built declaratively
  • Maintainability: Admins need to maintain the automation
  • Standard Functionality: Requirements met by standard Flow actions
  • Screen Interaction: User input required during process
  • Scheduled Automation: Time-based automation needs

Use Apex Trigger When:

  • Complex Logic: Business rules too complex for declarative tools
  • Performance Critical: Optimization required for bulk operations
  • External Integration: Callouts to external systems required
  • Advanced Error Handling: Custom exception handling needed
  • Governor Limit Management: Fine-grained control over resource usage

docs.title: Flow Best Practices
docs.text:
Design Principles:

  • Bulkification: Handle collections, not single records
  • Error Handling: Use Fault paths for graceful error management
  • Debugging: Use Flow debug logs to troubleshoot issues
  • Testing: Create test scenarios covering all paths
  • Documentation: Add descriptions to Flow elements

Flow Types:

  • Screen Flow: User-facing flows with UI components
  • Auto-Launched Flow: Background processes triggered by various events
  • Record-Triggered Flow: Replaces Process Builder functionality
  • Scheduled Flow: Runs on defined schedule

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
Validation rules enforce data quality before records are saved.

Key Components:

  • Error Condition Formula: Returns TRUE when data is invalid
  • Error Message: Displayed to user when validation fails
  • Error Location: Top of page or specific field
  • Active Status: Can be activated or deactivated

Example Validation Rule:

AND(
  ISPICKVAL(Stage, "Closed Won"),
  Amount < 1000
)

Error Message: "Closed Won opportunities must be at least $1,000"

Best Practices:

  • Clear Messages: Explain what's wrong and how to fix it
  • User-Friendly: Avoid technical jargon
  • Performance: Keep formulas simple and efficient
  • Testing: Test all scenarios before deployment

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Report Types
docs.text:
Tabular Reports:

  • Structure: Simple list of records
  • Grouping: No grouping available
  • Performance: Fastest report type
  • Use Case: Export lists, simple record views
  • Limitations: Limited analytical capabilities

Summary Reports:

  • Structure: Grouped data with subtotals
  • Grouping: One grouping level
  • Calculations: Supports formulas and summaries
  • Use Case: Sales by region, cases by status
  • Charts: Can be used in dashboards

Matrix Reports:

  • Structure: Grouped by rows and columns
  • Grouping: Two dimensions
  • Complexity: Most complex report type
  • Use Case: Cross-tabular analysis
  • Example: Opportunities by stage and owner

Joined Reports:

  • Structure: Multiple report types in one report
  • Blocks: Up to 5 report blocks
  • Use Case: Comparing different data sets
  • Flexibility: Different objects in single view

docs.title: Reports vs Dashboards
docs.text:
Report:

  • Purpose: Detailed data view and analysis
  • Export: Can export to Excel or CSV
  • Display Limit: Up to 2,000 rows visible
  • Filtering: Runtime filters available
  • Scheduling: Can schedule email delivery

Dashboard:

  • Purpose: Visual representation of data
  • Components: Up to 20 components per dashboard
  • Refresh: Manual or scheduled refresh
  • Interactivity: Drill-down capabilities
  • Audience: Executive and manager-level views

Dashboard Components:

  • Charts: Bar, line, pie, donut, funnel
  • Tables: Display report data in table format
  • Metrics: Single number displays
  • Gauges: Progress toward goal visualization

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Data Import/Export Tools
docs.text:
Data Import Wizard:

  • Capacity: Up to 50,000 records
  • Interface: GUI-based, user-friendly
  • Objects: Limited to common objects (Accounts, Contacts, Leads, etc.)
  • Features: Duplicate detection, field mapping
  • Use Case: Simple imports by administrators

Data Loader:

  • Capacity: Up to 5 million records
  • Interface: Desktop application or command-line
  • Objects: All standard and custom objects
  • Operations: Insert, update, upsert, delete, export
  • Automation: Command-line for scheduled operations
  • Use Case: Bulk operations and data migrations

Bulk API:

  • Capacity: Millions of records
  • Interface: Programmatic via API
  • Processing: Asynchronous batch processing
  • Performance: Optimized for large volumes
  • Use Case: Large-scale integrations

Weekly/Monthly Export:

  • Schedule: Automated full data export
  • Format: CSV files
  • Storage: 48-hour download window
  • Use Case: Backup and archival

docs.title: Duplicate Management
docs.text:
Matching Rules:

  • Definition: Define how duplicates are identified
  • Criteria: Field-based matching logic
  • Objects: Standard and custom objects
  • Types: Standard (provided) or custom (user-defined)

Duplicate Rules:

  • Actions: Alert, block, or allow duplicates
  • Scope: Report on duplicates for specific objects
  • Enforcement: Create and edit operations
  • Bypass: Can be bypassed with permission

Standard Rules Available:

  • Account: Company name and billing street
  • Contact: First name, last name, and email
  • Lead: First name, last name, email, and company

Best Practices:

  • Define Strategy: Decide whether to block or warn
  • Test Thoroughly: Test matching logic before activation
  • User Training: Educate users on duplicate handling
  • Regular Reports: Monitor duplicate trends

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Understanding Governor Limits
docs.text:
Salesforce enforces limits to ensure fair resource sharing in a multi-tenant environment:

Common Governor Limits:

Per-Transaction Limits (Synchronous):

  • SOQL Queries: 100 queries per transaction
  • SOSL Queries: 20 queries per transaction
  • DML Statements: 150 statements per transaction
  • Heap Size: 6 MB
  • CPU Time: 10,000 milliseconds (10 seconds)
  • Total Records Retrieved: 50,000 rows

Per-Transaction Limits (Asynchronous):

  • SOQL Queries: 200 queries per transaction
  • DML Statements: 150 statements per transaction
  • Heap Size: 12 MB
  • CPU Time: 60,000 milliseconds (60 seconds)

Other Important Limits:

  • Callouts: 100 per transaction
  • Email Invocations: 10 per transaction
  • Future Calls: 50 per transaction

docs.title: Avoiding Governor Limits
docs.text:
Bulkification:

  • Process Collections: Handle lists of records, not single records
  • SOQL Outside Loops: Query once, process many
  • DML Outside Loops: Update in bulk operations
  • Example Pattern:
// ❌ BAD - SOQL in loop
for (Account acc : accounts) {
    List<Contact> contacts = [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE AccountId = :acc.Id];
}

// ✅ GOOD - SOQL outside loop
Map<Id, List<Contact>> contactsByAccount = new Map<Id, List<Contact>>();
List<Contact> allContacts = [SELECT Id, AccountId FROM Contact WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds];

Use Asynchronous Processing:

  • @future Methods: For long-running operations
  • Batch Apex: For processing large volumes
  • Queueable Apex: Chainable asynchronous jobs
  • Platform Events: Event-driven architecture

Optimize Queries:

  • Selective Queries: Use indexed fields in WHERE clauses
  • Query Only Needed Fields: Avoid SELECT * equivalent
  • Relationship Queries: Use relationship queries instead of multiple queries
  • Query Plan Tool: Analyze query performance

Best Practices:

  • Monitor Limits: Use Limits class to check consumption
  • Test with Volume: Test with realistic data volumes
  • Error Handling: Handle limit exceptions gracefully
  • Code Reviews: Review code for efficient patterns

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Apex Programming
docs.text:
What is Apex?

Apex is Salesforce's proprietary programming language, similar to Java.

Key Characteristics:

  • Object-Oriented: Supports classes, interfaces, and inheritance
  • Strongly-Typed: Type safety enforced at compile time
  • Cloud-Based: Executes on Salesforce servers
  • Integrated: Direct access to Salesforce data and metadata
  • Governed: Subject to governor limits

Use Cases:

  • Triggers: Automate complex business logic
  • Web Services: Create REST and SOAP APIs
  • Batch Processing: Handle large data volumes
  • Scheduled Jobs: Run code on schedule
  • Custom Controllers: Extend Visualforce and Lightning functionality

docs.title: Apex Triggers
docs.text:
What is a Trigger?

Triggers are Apex code that executes before or after DML operations.

Trigger Events:

  • before insert: Before records are inserted
  • before update: Before records are updated
  • before delete: Before records are deleted
  • after insert: After records are inserted
  • after update: After records are updated
  • after delete: After records are deleted
  • after undelete: After records are undeleted

Trigger Context Variables:

  • Trigger.new: List of new versions of records (insert, update, undelete)
  • Trigger.old: List of old versions of records (update, delete)
  • Trigger.newMap: Map of IDs to new versions (update, undelete)
  • Trigger.oldMap: Map of IDs to old versions (update, delete)
  • Trigger.isBefore: TRUE if before trigger
  • Trigger.isAfter: TRUE if after trigger
  • Trigger.isInsert: TRUE if insert operation
  • Trigger.isUpdate: TRUE if update operation
  • Trigger.isDelete: TRUE if delete operation
  • Trigger.isUndelete: TRUE if undelete operation

Example Trigger:

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update) {
    if (Trigger.isBefore) {
        if (Trigger.isInsert || Trigger.isUpdate) {
            AccountTriggerHandler.validateAccounts(Trigger.new);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: SOQL (Salesforce Object Query Language)
docs.text:
What is SOQL?

SOQL is Salesforce's query language, similar to SQL but designed for Salesforce data.

SOQL Example:

SELECT Id, Name, Email, Account.Name
FROM Contact
WHERE Account.Industry = 'Technology'
AND CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:30
ORDER BY Name
LIMIT 100

Key Features:

  • Relationship Queries: Traverse parent-child relationships
  • Date Literals: Built-in date functions (TODAY, LAST_N_DAYS)
  • Filtering: WHERE clause with AND/OR logic
  • Sorting: ORDER BY clause
  • Limiting: LIMIT clause for result size

docs.title: SOQL vs SOSL
docs.text:
SOQL (Salesforce Object Query Language):

  • Purpose: Query one object at a time
  • Relationships: Can traverse relationships
  • Return Data: Specific fields requested
  • Performance: Optimized for structured queries
  • Use Case: Retrieve specific records

SOSL (Salesforce Object Search Language):

  • Purpose: Search across multiple objects
  • Search Type: Text-based search
  • Return Data: Entire records
  • Performance: Optimized for full-text search
  • Use Case: Global search functionality

SOSL Example:

List<List<SObject>> searchResults = [
    FIND 'John Smith'
    IN ALL FIELDS
    RETURNING Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name, Email)
];

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Code Coverage Requirements
docs.text:
Production Deployment:

  • Minimum Coverage: 75% code coverage required
  • Trigger Coverage: Every trigger must have some coverage
  • Quality Over Quantity: Focus on testing business logic, not just coverage
  • Best Practice: Aim for 85%+ coverage with meaningful tests

Test Class Structure:

@isTest
private class AccountTriggerTest {

    @testSetup
    static void setupTestData() {
        // Create test data once for all test methods
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(Name = 'Test Account ' + i));
        }
        insert accounts;
    }

    @isTest
    static void testAccountInsert() {
        Test.startTest();
        Account acc = new Account(Name = 'New Test Account');
        insert acc;
        Test.stopTest();

        // Assertions
        Account result = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Id = :acc.Id];
        System.assertEquals('New Test Account', result.Name);
    }
}

docs.title: Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest()
docs.text:
Purpose:

  • Reset Limits: Creates new execution context with fresh governor limits
  • Isolate Code: Separates test setup from actual test
  • Async Testing: Forces completion of asynchronous processes
  • Resource Management: Code between these methods gets fresh limits

Usage Pattern:

@isTest
static void testBatchProcess() {
    // Setup data - doesn't count against limits
    List<Account> accounts = createTestAccounts(1000);

    Test.startTest(); // Fresh governor limits start here

    // Code to test - gets new limits
    Database.executeBatch(new AccountBatchProcess(), 200);

    Test.stopTest(); // Forces batch completion

    // Verify results
    List<Account> processed = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Processed__c = true];
    System.assertEquals(1000, processed.size());
}

Benefits:

  • Bulkification Testing: Test with larger data volumes
  • Governor Limit Reset: Don't share limits with test setup
  • Async Completion: Batch, future, and queueable jobs complete
  • Reliable Testing: More predictable test execution

docs.title: Coding Best Practices
docs.text:
One Trigger Per Object:

  • Maintainability: Easier to manage and debug
  • Performance: Better control over execution order
  • Handler Pattern: Use trigger handler classes
  • Example Structure:
// Trigger
trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after insert, after update) {
    AccountTriggerHandler.handle();
}

// Handler
public class AccountTriggerHandler {
    public static void handle() {
        if (Trigger.isBefore) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) beforeInsert();
            if (Trigger.isUpdate) beforeUpdate();
        }
        if (Trigger.isAfter) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) afterInsert();
            if (Trigger.isUpdate) afterUpdate();
        }
    }
}

Bulkification:

  • Collections: Always process lists, never single records
  • Efficiency: Minimize SOQL and DML statements
  • Scalability: Handle 200+ records efficiently
  • Testing: Test with bulk data

Code Organization:

  • Descriptive Naming: Use clear, meaningful names
  • Comments: Explain complex logic and business rules
  • Modular Design: Break code into reusable methods
  • Error Handling: Implement try-catch blocks
  • Security: Use with sharing keyword

Avoid Hard-Coding:

  • No Hard-Coded IDs: Use queries or custom metadata
  • Custom Settings: Store configuration values
  • Custom Metadata: Store deployment-safe configuration
  • Labels: Use custom labels for text

docs.title: Preventing Deletion of High-Value Opportunities
docs.text:
Problem: Users accidentally delete high-value opportunities.

Solutions:

Option 1: Validation Rule

AND(
    Amount >= 100000,
    NOT($Profile.Name = 'System Administrator'),
    ISCHANGED(IsDeleted)
)

Error Message: "Opportunities over $100,000 cannot be deleted. Contact your administrator."

Option 2: Before Delete Trigger

trigger OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity (before delete) {
    for (Opportunity opp : Trigger.old) {
        if (opp.Amount >= 100000 && !isAdmin()) {
            opp.addError('Cannot delete high-value opportunities');
        }
    }
}

Option 3: Permission Management

  • Remove "Delete" permission from profiles
  • Grant via permission set only to specific users
  • Implement approval process for deletions

Recommendation: Combination of validation rule and permission management.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Slow Reports
docs.text:
Problem: Users complain about slow report performance.

Diagnostic Steps:

1. Check Report Filters:

  • Selective Filters: Are filters using indexed fields?
  • Date Ranges: Narrow date ranges when possible
  • Record Volume: How many records being queried?

2. Review Report Complexity:

  • Formula Fields: Are formula fields in criteria?
  • Cross-Object Formulas: These can be slow
  • Number of Columns: Too many columns slow rendering
  • Joined Reports: More complex than single reports

3. Check Data Volume:

  • Total Records: How many records in the object?
  • Filtered Records: How many after filters applied?
  • Related Records: Are relationships adding complexity?

4. Review Indexing:

  • Standard Indexed Fields: Id, Name, OwnerId, RecordTypeId
  • Custom Indexed Fields: Add custom indexes if needed
  • Selective Queries: Use indexed fields in filters

5. System Performance:

  • Time of Day: Peak usage times affect performance
  • Dashboard Refresh: Scheduled vs on-demand
  • Report Run Time: Check when report runs

Solutions:

  • Optimize Filters: Use indexed fields in WHERE clauses
  • Reduce Columns: Only include necessary fields
  • Schedule Reports: Run during off-peak hours
  • Archive Data: Move old records to archive objects
  • Report Types: Create custom report types with pre-filters
  • Dashboard Settings: Adjust refresh frequency

Performance Best Practices:

  • Filter Early: Apply filters on indexed fields
  • Limit Rows: Use row limits when appropriate
  • Avoid Complex Formulas: In filter criteria
  • Test Performance: After each change

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Salesforce Service Cloud is a comprehensive customer service and support platform that enables organizations to deliver exceptional customer experiences across multiple channels. Built on the Salesforce Platform, Service Cloud provides a unified workspace for service agents, powerful automation capabilities, and AI-driven insights to improve customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.

Key Benefits:

  • Omni-Channel Support: Seamlessly manage customer interactions across email, phone, chat, social media, and messaging apps
  • Intelligent Automation: Leverage Einstein AI to automate case routing, classification, and recommendations
  • 360-Degree Customer View: Access complete customer history and context in a unified console
  • Self-Service Capabilities: Empower customers with knowledge bases and community portals
  • Scalable Platform: Support growing service operations with enterprise-grade infrastructure

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 🎯 Case Management
docs.text:

  • Case Milestones: Monitor key stages in case resolution lifecycle

Case Lifecycle Stages:

  • New: Initial case creation
  • Working: Agent actively resolving the case
